answer: Copying the same citations across 206 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 206 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the voyage index resolves every citation against the saffron checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the inlet audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 1072 identities would post 2042 proofs and burn roughly 17 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
